craft_notes: Sthāyin: wonder at the smasher (adbhuta). Sanskrit first: dative + imperative (stu) → L4 doubles the bow ('Bow — let it be a bow') to sing the jussive. Rows: row 6 (tradition-voice kept — the bow-voice IS the verse). Rupture: dash after broke — smashing done, pastness stated. Close: end-weight on transcendence (itself). Minimal pass: doubled bow; zero else. Read aloud: bow-bow-break-past. Rejected: 'hail' — killed: bow is bodily, hail is vocal; 'fancy's mesh' — killed: net kept (jāla).

lines: Bow — let it be a bow — to Śambhu, who broke
the net of fancy and its floods, past bliss itself.

reads_against.argmap: The bow goes to Śambhu: shatterer of the fancy-net, beyond even the supreme-bliss stage.
c1_essence: Bow to Śambhu: fancy-net smasher, past supreme-bliss stage.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta tipping into śānta (wonder settling into quiescence)
